source_caption: A wealthy New York socialite is unexpectedly put in charge of her father’s struggling hip-hop record label, forcing her into a world far removed from the one she knows. As she attempts to save the business, she butts heads with its outspoken biggest artist, leading to culture clashes, unlikely alliances, and a romance that neither of them sees coming. Balancing sharp satire with lighthearted comedy, Marci X explores fame, identity, and the unlikely connections that emerge when two completely different worlds collide.

source_details.title: Marci X
source_details.synopsis: Marci X is a 2003 American romantic comedy film directed by Richard Benjamin, written by Paul Rudnick, and starring Lisa Kudrow as Jewish-American Princess Marci Feld, who has to take control of a hip-hop record label, as well as the controversial rapper Dr. S, played by Damon Wayans. The film was released on August 22, 2003, by Paramount Pictures. It received negative reviews and was a box office flop, grossing $1.7 million worldwide against a $20 million budget.
